correctness.rationale: The explicit GP(10,2) dodecahedron (20 vertices) and 12-vertex icosahedron define all edges without pictorial ambiguity. Singletons stall because each initially observed neighbor has two unobserved neighbors. Completely enumerating 190 and 66 two-vertex seed sets by deterministic closed-neighborhood plus simultaneous unique-neighbor propagation proves: only dodecahedral distance-three pairs succeed (60), every icosahedral pair succeeds (66). For D the distance-three adjacency graph is six-regular; optimal-set exchange graph is its line graph (60 vertices, 300 edges). Full BFS determines distances (300,870,600), diameter three; I exchange graph is L(K12) (66 vertices, 660 edges, diameter two). Our separately implemented bitmask and set propagation and independent BFS reproduced all 256 cases. Since the target graphs are fixed finite objects, the complete census is a finite proof, not extrapolation.
